Ciliary regulatory mechanism in proteostasis and cell-death pathway:

This schematic shows the role of cilia in regulating proteostasis and cell-death pathways, including autophagy and apoptosis, underscoring their importance in health and disease. A. Cilia contribute to the maintenance of proteostasis through mechanisms such as chaperone-mediated protein folding and degradation pathways, including the ubiquitin-proteasome system. B. Role of cilia in modulating apoptotic signals, indicating how ciliary dysfunction can lead to disrupted apoptotic pathways and contribute to cell survival or death. C. Autophagy plays a significant role in the process of ciliogenesis. Varying nutrient environments can influence autophagy processes, which in turn affect the formation and function of cilia. D. Illustrates the process of autophagy as a ciliary response to a signal, detailing how ciliary signaling can enhance autophagosome formation and degradation of damaged organelles and proteins
